title: Same recipe, three fates
view: three whole 256^2 periodic worlds, 2 px per cell

scan.classes: died: mass < 0.05 x one Orbium; filled: fill (A > 0.1) > 0.15; otherwise 'k orbium-mass' with k = round(mass / one Orbium's mass) (a mass count, not an identification)

picked: the first seed of each class in seed order (not the prettiest)
caveats: One noise recipe (80x80, uniform [0, 0.3)), one rule (S001), one world size; the counts are for this recipe only. Most other amplitudes we tried in a 6-seed pilot died out entirely.
'Orbium-sized survivor' is a mass count; the film shows what it is for the picked seed only.
The world-filling outcome resembles the reef lattice (G008) but happens here under the S001 rule, not the coexistence rule; we have not compared the two lattices.
Random initial states as a way to find Lenia creatures are standard practice (Chan 2019); not novel.

runs.initial_state: 80x80 square of uniform [0, 0.3) noise, numpy default_rng(0).random, centred on zero 256^2
80x80 square of uniform [0, 0.3) noise, numpy default_rng(5).random, centred on zero 256^2
80x80 square of uniform [0, 0.3) noise, numpy default_rng(1).random, centred on zero 256^2

render.colormap: matplotlib inferno, A in [0,1] mapped linearly, nearest-neighbour

reproduce: git checkout <this commit> && .venv/bin/python research/experiments/VIS-talk/film.py G010   # verify only: film.py verify G010
